title: Evaluate the inner value
text: First, calculate the inner value: what is $$\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)?$$

title: Identify the quadrant
text: Observe that $$\frac{5\pi}{4}=\pi+\frac{\pi}{4},$$ which is in the third quadrant.

subHints.title: Remember the range
subHints.text: The output of $$\arcsin$$ must be in the principal range $$\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right].$$ $$\frac{5\pi}{4}$$ is outside this range.

subHints.title: Connection to the unit circle
subHints.text: Recall that $$\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{4}\right)$$ represents the $$y-$$ coordinate of the point on the unit circle at the angle $$\frac{5\pi}{4}.$$

subHints.title: Find equivalent angle geometrically
subHints.text: The principal range of $$\arcsin$$ is $$\left[\frac{-\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right], $$ which is the right half of the unit circle. To find an angle in this range with the same $$y-$$ coordinate as $$\frac{5\pi}{4}, $$ imagine drawing a horizontal line straight across from Quadrant III into Quadrant IV. This line hits the right half of the circle at $$\frac{-\pi}{4}.$$\n##figure1.gif##

subHints.title: Find equivalent angle algebraically
subHints.text: We can also solve this algebraically. The angle $$\frac{5\pi}{4}$$ has a reference angle of $$\frac{\pi}{4}$$ and lies in Quadrant III, where sine is negative. The only quadrant in our principal range where sine is also negative is Quadrant IV. The angle in Quadrant IV with a reference angle of $$\frac{\pi}{4}$$ is $$\frac{-\pi}{4}.$$
